title: Retargeting Video Ad Template | AIVideosUGC
description: Bring viewed products back with a retargeting video from one photo. Show a clear detail, add a confirmed offer after download, and post where they shop.
h1: Retargeting Video Ad for Shoppers Who Already Looked
lead: Someone who opened your skillet listing can see a new clip about the handle. Start from a follow-up layout and put that skillet back on screen. You are not writing a prompt from a blank box.
steps_h2: How to Make a Retargeting Video Ad in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: The lamp they already viewed goes back on screen, with a line about the part they skipped.

steps.d: Use the listing photo of the lamp they paused on. The follow-up layout already expects a product the shopper has met.
Name what the first visit skipped: this lamp's dimmer. An avatar you pick for the shop says that line.
Save the file and show it to people who visited the lamp page. The ad account controls how often lamp visitors see it.

faq.q: What is a retargeting video template?
faq.a: It is a follow-up clip for a product the shopper already opened. The kettle comes back on screen so the line can talk about the whistle, and you skip booking a second shoot to say it.

faq.q: How does a retargeting template get made into an ad?
faq.a: You leave with a file you can publish to people who already visited. Take the skillet they viewed, point the line at the riveted handle, and export a square for the placement that brought them in.

faq.q: Why template a follow-up instead of filming a creator again?
faq.a: Filming the creator again puts the reminder on their calendar. When the headphone sale changes, you rewrite the offer in this follow-up and send the new file to people who already watched the first ad.

faq.q: Who is a follow-up template for?
faq.a: The person who buys media for a shop, and the owner who answers those ads herself. A candle shop running a second touch on yesterday's visitors is the usual case, and a small agency can do the same for a few shops.

faq.q: Can someone new to video make the follow-up?
faq.a: Yes. Starting from the product-page photo, the three steps get you a follow-up in a few minutes.

faq.q: Which shops can run a second-touch ad from this layout?
faq.a: Shops that already have visitors to talk to again. A wool-throw store, a phone-case brand, and a bakery shipping tins can each keep the layout and change the line to the product those visitors opened.

faq.q: Can the ad use photos and clips I already own?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the toaster identical to the listing they already opened. Your logo can mark the corner, and a clip of the lever is welcome if you filmed one.

faq.q: Which placements is the template shaped for?
faq.a: Aim the follow-up at the placement that earned the first visit. A Facebook return can use 4:3, TikTok can take 9:16, the shop grid can take 1:1, and YouTube or LinkedIn can take 16:9 or 3:4.

faq.q: Does a retargeting template require payment?
faq.a: Yes. Access sits on a paid subscription. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits, Pro is $35 with 300, and Premium is $63 with 600. Video credits are 24, 40, 60, or 120 for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. The cost shows first, and a failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: Can I run this follow-up in paid ads and send it to a client?
faq.a: Yes. Send it back to people who visited, put it on the fan's product page, or pass the file to a client who sells that fan.

faq.q: Why use a retargeting video template?
faq.a: You spend the effort on the reminder, not on inventing a structure. The wool throw they already viewed keeps this layout, and only the line about the weave is new.
